Rahn is not covered in saa.pdf (its ten include Wadiah instead). Rahn's anchor is Qur'an 2:283 — explicit.
Not named in the Qur'an. Rests on the general permission of trade (Q2:275) and mutual consent (Q4:29).
No murabaha-specific hadith — governed by the general sale rules, e.g. the sale-option hadith.
Al-Tabari's commentary on Q2:275 fixes the trade-vs-riba distinction murabaha rests on.
Al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an) develops the same trade/riba reading of Q2:275.
Al-Shafi'i's Kitab al-Umm holds the seminal passage: 'buy this and I will give you a profit — this deal is lawful' — the trust-sale (cost disclosed) foundation later used for bank murabaha.
Al-Kasani (Bada'i al-Sana'i) gives the standard definition: 'sale for a price similar to the first price plus an excess as profit'.
Ibn Qudama (al-Mughni) treats murabaha among the named sales for the Hanbali school; Malik and the Hanafis do likewise.
Sami Hamoud engineers 'Murabaha to the Purchase Orderer' in his Cairo PhD, grounding the bank three-party structure on al-Shafi'i's passage; recommends it to IsDB and Dubai Islamic Bank.
Hamoud's model applied in practice at Jordan Islamic Bank (1978-79).
OIC Fiqh Academy Resolutions 40-41 (5th session, Kuwait) make the customer's promise binding — the legal key to bank murabaha.
OIC Fiqh Academy declares organized tawarruq (reverse murabaha) impermissible.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 8 codifies murabaha for the industry.
Dominates bank financing: 80-90% of some banks' operations (IIBI est.); >55% GCC average 2016. Criticized (Abdullah Saeed) as replicating interest.
No direct verse. Jurists cite the shared root 'darb fi'l-ard' (Q73:20; 2:198; 62:10) as wording-level support only. Ibn Hazm: qirad rests on consensus, not text.
The Prophet traded for Khadija on qirad terms before prophethood and approved the practice.

'Blessing is in three: credit sale, silent partnership (muqaradah), mixing wheat with barley for the home.' Grading of this narration is debated. Validity rests mainly on Companion practice: Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Aisha invested orphans' funds by mudarabah.
Commentary attaches to the darb-fi'l-ard verses but treats the link as wording only, not a legal proof.
Malik's al-Muwatta, Kitab al-Qirad (Book 32): earliest systematic record — Uthman's qirad deal and the episode of Umar's sons trading public money.
Al-Sarakhsi (al-Mabsut) gives the fullest early Hanafi treatment of mudarabah.
Al-Kasani: strict analogy would forbid mudarabah (undefined labor/wages) — it stands by consensus and need.
Ibn Qudama (al-Mughni) treats it extensively for the Hanbalis.

rows.work: Partnership and Profit-Sharing in Islamic Law
rows.detail: Siddiqi's 'Partnership and Profit-Sharing in Islamic Law' — the seminal modern theory; basis of two-tier deposit banking.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 13 codifies mudarabah (investment/savings deposits).
Partnership recognized, not legislated: Q38:24 ('many partners wrong one another...') and Q4:12 ('partners in a third'). Root SH-R-K.
Qudsi hadith: 'I am the third of two partners as long as neither betrays the other.' The Prophet also approved pre-Islamic partnerships.
Al-Qurtubi on Q38:24 and 4:12 discusses co-mingling (khultah) and its rules.
Al-Sarakhsi (al-Mabsut): fullest Hanafi treatment; shirkah split into ownership vs contract, with subtypes 'inan, mufawada, abdan, wujuh.
Al-Kasani (Bada'i) completes the Hanafi doctrine of partnership types.
Ibn Rushd (Bidayat al-Mujtahid) supplies the comparative four-school picture of shirkah.
'Diminishing musharakah' engineered for home finance; promoted by Siddiqi as the ideal profit-and-loss alternative to interest.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 12 (Sharikah and Modern Corporations).
Small in practice: 0.8% of 2022 sukuk issuance vs wakala 27.3%, murabaha 24.8% (IFSB 2023).
Explicit basis: Q65:6 (pay the wages), Q28:26-27 ('hire him — the best you can hire is the strong and trustworthy'), Q18:77 (a wage for the wall). Root a-j-r.
'Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.'
Qudsi: Allah is the adversary of one who hires a laborer, takes full work, and does not pay. The Prophet also hired a Banu al-Dayl guide for the Hijra and paid the cupper his wage.
Al-Tabari on Q28:26 and 65:6 establishes hire/wage legitimacy and conditions.
Al-Razi's commentary adds the conditions analysis.
Ibn Rushd (Bidayat al-Mujtahid): comparative validation — all four schools accept ijarah by Qur'an, Sunnah and consensus; notes only Ibn al-Asamm rejected leasing as uncertain.
Ibn Qudama (al-Mughni, vol. VI): the detailed Hanbali rulebook of leasing; Maliki/Hanbali add the 'lawful benefits' limit.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 9: ijarah + lease-ending-in-ownership (IMB) — engine of asset finance and ijarah sukuk.
Ijarah = 16.9% of 2022 sukuk issuance (IFSB 2023).
Tied to the verse of debt Q2:282 ('write it down'); Ibn Abbas: this verse was revealed regarding salam.

The clearest contract hadith of all ten: at Medina, 'whoever pays in advance, let it be for a known measure, known weight, and a fixed term.' Practiced under Abu Bakr and Umar; the canonical exception to selling what you do not possess.
Al-Tabari links Q2:282's debt-documentation to salam.

Treated as a distinct valid sale with strict conditions from Malik's Muwatta onward (al-Umm, al-Mabsut, Bada'i, al-Mughni all follow); schools differ on market availability between contract and delivery.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 10 (Salam and Parallel Salam); salam sukuk by Bahrain and The Gambia.
No direct verse — only the general trade permission (Q2:275).
No istisna hadith. The Prophet's ring and pulpit being made are cited as indicative practice only, not authority.

Al-Kasani (Bada'i 5/2), the decisive text: 'By analogy istisna is not permissible... but it is allowed by istihsan because people have consensus of practice on it.' A Hanafi contract; other schools folded it into salam; late Hanafis made it binding on both sides.
OIC Fiqh Academy Resolution 65 (3/7) makes istisna binding when subject, specs and price are fixed. YEAR CONFLICT: source doc says 1988; standard references say the 7th session was 1992 — verify.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 11 (Istisna'a and Parallel Istisna'a) — project and housing finance.
Q18:19 ('send one of you with this silver coin...') and Q12:55 ('appoint me over the storehouses') — delegation recognized. Root w-k-l.
The Prophet appointed agents: Urwah al-Bariqi to buy a sacrificial animal; 'Amr ibn Umayya to contract his marriage; agents to collect zakat; Jabir took dates from the Prophet's agent at Khaybar.
Al-Qurtubi on Q18:19: 'send/appoint' (ib'athu) as a basis for agency.
Ibn Rushd lists the four pillars of agency: principal, agent, subject matter, formula.
Ibn Qudama (al-Mughni 5:71) treats agency incl. the fuduli (unauthorized agent awaiting ratification); al-Kasani likewise.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 23 (Agency). Investment agency (wakalah bi'l-istithmar) becomes the workhorse of deposits, sukuk and takaful.
The single largest sukuk structure: 27.3% of 2022 issuance (IFSB 2023).

Q12:72: 'whoever brings it will have a camel-load, and I am responsible for it (wa ana bihi za'im)' — za'im read as guarantor by Ibn Abbas; 12:66 and 12:78 also cited. Same verse anchors ju'alah (reward).
The Prophet refused to pray over a man who died in debt until Abu Qatada said 'I undertake his debt' — then prayed.
'Whoever dies in debt among the believers, I am responsible for its repayment.'

rows.citation_collection: Sunan Abu Dawud; Tirmidhi; Ibn Majah
rows.detail: The maxim 'al-za'im gharim' (the guarantor is liable) — NOT in Bukhari; it is in the Sunan.
Adjacent hawala anchor: 'Delay by a wealthy debtor is injustice; if your debt is transferred to a solvent person, accept it.'
Al-Tabari and later al-Qurtubi treat za'im in Q12:72 as guarantor.
Kitab al-Kafalah/al-Daman in all schools; Ibn Qudama (al-Mughni 5:71) and al-Kasani set out the two types: guarantee of person and of property.
OIC Fiqh Academy 2nd Session (Jeddah, Dec 1985): no fee may be charged on an uncovered guarantee — the rule behind today's kafalah-fee dispute.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 5 (Guarantees) — bank guarantees, letters of credit, takaful.
Explicit: 'qard hasan' appears in six verses (2:245; 5:12; 57:11; 57:18; 64:17; 73:20), always a loan 'to Allah'; 2:282 governs recording.
'Every loan is charity'; lending twice equals giving once. The Prophet borrowed and repaid better, and pledged his armor to a Jewish merchant for barley — the same narration that anchors RAHN.
Ibn Kathir on 57:11 and 64:17: the loan 'to Allah' as charitable spending with guaranteed manifold repayment.
Universal from the earliest fiqh: qard is a gratuitous contract; ANY stipulated increase is riba; repay exactly the principal.
AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 19 (Qard) — microfinance, current accounts; voluntary extra repayment allowed if unstipulated.
Q2:283 ('let the trustee discharge his trust') and Q4:58 ('render trusts to whom they are due'). Roots amana + wada'a.
'Render the trust to the one who entrusted you; do not betray the one who betrayed you.' Plus: no liability on a non-negligent trustee.
Al-Tabari and al-Qurtubi on 2:283 and 4:58: the duty to return deposits.
Kitab al-Wadi'a: the schools split custody into pure trust (yad amanah) vs guaranteed custody (yad damanah, custodian may use the asset); Hanafis two pillars, majority three.
No early standalone AAOIFI standard; Bank Negara Malaysia issues a dedicated Wadi'ah policy. Guaranteed custody becomes the basis of Islamic current/savings accounts with a discretionary gift.
